title: Horse equipment — overseas racing English-Japanese dictionary
covers: Noseband; Ear plug; Pacifier; Bit; Reins; Breastplate; Martingale; Horseshoe
note: JRA maps current overseas-racing equipment labels including nose band, ear plug, pacifier, bit, reins, breast plate, martingale and horseshoe to Japanese racing terms. Use for label identity; functional claims require separate evidence.

title: Past Performance Information — medication and equipment codes
covers: Bar Shoes; Glued Shoes; No Shoes; No Whip
note: Equibase lists Bar Shoes, Glued Shoes, No Shoes and No Whip as distinct equipment codes in North American past-performance information. Use as regional operational equipment terminology.

title: Equipped for Racing
note: USTA directly explains ear plugs and whip use in harness racing and identifies the racebike as the sulky. Use for Harness-specific meaning rather than universal equipment rules.

title: Current Gear / Gear Changes — 2026 fields
covers: Pacifiers; Ear Muffs; Nose Band; Bits
note: Current 2026 Racing Australia field/gear displays use Pacifiers, Ear Muffs, Cross-over Nose Band, Lugging Bit and related gear as operational racing equipment. Exact construction and approval rules remain jurisdiction-specific.

title: Race terminology — overseas racing English-Japanese dictionary
note: JRA maps schooling to スクーリング／事前下見 and warm up to 返し馬 in overseas-racing context. Definitions stay at that supported semantic level.

title: Gallop — overseas racing English-Japanese dictionary
note: JRA maps gallop to ギャロップ／襲歩 in the training vocabulary. Use for the training-gait label without imposing a universal workout intensity.

title: Current 2026 qualifier conditions / qualifying race cards
note: Current USTA-produced condition sheets explicitly schedule QUALIFIERS and publish qualifying standards; USTA results also denote qualifying cards as Qua. Use for the North American Harness qualifying-event sense.

title: Racetrack Experience
note: USTA explains that horses warm up on the track between races and are introduced on the track in the post parade before the start. Use for North American Harness pre-race terminology.

title: Racing Explained — Glossary
note: The Jockey Club defines Going Down as horses on their way to the start, saying they are going down to post. Use as British racing pre-start terminology.

title: Racing 101 — Glossary of Terms
note: Racing Victoria defines Spell as a horse having a minimum two-month (60-day) break from racing. Keep that duration attached to Victoria/Australian glossary usage rather than universalizing it.
